title: Fire recall check: Soundcore 3 and older Mitsubishi Heavy air conditioners still have many units unrecovered
summary: Consumer Affairs Agency flagged fresh fire reports on September 1 involving two already-recalled product groups. If may Soundcore 3 ka or an older Mitsubishi Heavy Industries aircon, check the model now: affected Soundcore 3 units are being collected/replaced, while affected 1999-2007 aircons get free inspection/repair. Official recovery rates remain only 44.0% and 9.8%, respectively.
why_it_matters: This is not a theoretical recall reminder. The September 1 government release reports new fires involving both product groups, although the causes of these latest incidents are still under investigation. The preventive action is free and the downside of ignoring a matching unit includes a plausible fire loss far above ¥10,000.

claims.text: The Consumer Affairs Agency published 19 serious product accidents on September 1, 2026 and specifically highlighted recalled air conditioners and a rechargeable speaker after fire reports.
The recalled Soundcore 3 group covers model A3117 variants sold from December 16, 2022 through October 21, 2025, totaling 91,933 units; the official recovery rate was 44.0% as of August 31, 2026.
claims.basis: CAA recall table and Anker recall notice

claims.text: CAA says the Soundcore 3 recall addresses a possibility of foreign material entering battery cells during supplier manufacturing, potentially causing internal short circuit and fire; users with an affected unrecovered unit are told to stop using it immediately and arrange collection/replacement.
claims.basis: Official recall reason and user instruction

claims.text: The Mitsubishi Heavy Industries air-conditioner recall covers certain units imported from October 1999 through 2007, approximately 930,000 units; only 9.8% had been repaired as of July 31, 2026. CAA says affected unrepaired units should be stopped and submitted for free inspection/repair.

The two newly reported air-conditioner fires and the newly reported Soundcore 3 fire are still under investigation, and CAA explicitly says it is not yet known whether these latest incidents were caused by the known recall defects.
Because a model check takes little effort, the recall remedy is free, and unrecovered populations remain large, checking matching household products now has unusually strong risk-reduction value.
claims.basis: Inference from free remedy, fire consequence and low recovery rates

reading_levels.30_sec: DO NOW: Check any Soundcore 3 and old Mitsubishi Heavy Industries aircon in the house. Soundcore 3 model A3117 variants in the affected sales period may qualify for free collection/replacement; certain Mitsubishi Heavy aircons imported 1999-2007 qualify for free inspection/repair. CAA reported fresh fires on September 1. Stop using a matching unrecovered unit and use the manufacturer recall channel.
reading_levels.2_min: For Soundcore 3, CAA lists black A3117011, navy A3117031, red A3117091 and gray A31170A1 variants under the A3117 recall group, sold December 16, 2022-October 21, 2025; 91,933 units were covered and only 44.0% had been recovered by August 31. For the older Mitsubishi Heavy air conditioners, about 930,000 units are in the recall population and the repair rate was only 9.8% by July 31. The latest reported fires are real, but their causes are still being investigated, so do not claim the recall defect caused them. The practical point is simpler: if your unit matches, the official instruction is to stop use and take the free remedy.
reading_levels.deep: The Soundcore 3 known recall mechanism is potential contamination during battery-cell manufacturing that can lead to internal short circuit and fire. CAA records three recall-related serious fires in FY2025 and three in FY2026 before the latest incident, which is not yet counted as confirmed recall-caused. For the Mitsubishi Heavy aircon group, the known recall concern involves a lead-wire connection for the indoor fan motor under certain conditions. The government release lists repeated historical fires in the recalled population and a very low repair rate. These facts justify urgent checking without overstating causation for the newest cases.

content.who_is_affected: Anyone in Japan who owns a Soundcore 3 from the affected A3117 variants/sales period, or certain Mitsubishi Heavy Industries air conditioners imported from October 1999 through 2007 that have not already received the recall remedy.
content.when: CAA issued the fresh accident warning on September 1, 2026. The recalls are already active; action should be immediate for a matching unrecovered unit.
content.financial_impact: No defensible household saving amount is assigned because the primary value is fire-risk reduction, not a discount. The official recall remedies are free collection/replacement for affected Soundcore 3 units and free inspection/repair for affected Mitsubishi Heavy air conditioners.
content.risk_if_ignored: Potential fire and property damage. The newest incidents are still under investigation, but both product groups already have active official recalls for fire-related hazards.
content.action: DO NOW — check the model/serial information. If your unit matches and has not received the remedy, stop using it and contact the official manufacturer recall channel for free replacement or inspection/repair.
content.deadline: No fixed end date is stated in the September 1 CAA notice; treat this as immediate because the hazard is safety-related and the recall remains active.
content.potential_benefit: Free remedy plus avoidance of a low-frequency but potentially severe fire/property-loss event.
content.downside: You may spend a few minutes checking a unit that turns out not to be affected, and replacement/repair logistics may cause temporary inconvenience. Do not assume every Soundcore 3 or every old Mitsubishi aircon is affected; verify the exact model/serial against the official recall information.
content.what_would_change_mind: Downgrade urgency only if the manufacturer confirms a specific unit is outside the affected population or has already received the remedy. Upgrade further if investigation confirms the newest fires were caused by the known recall defects or if additional incidents are reported.

pr_vs_reality.official_claim: CAA and the manufacturers instruct owners of affected unrecovered products to stop use and obtain the free recall remedy.
evidence_says: Both recalls concern mechanisms capable of causing fire, and substantial portions of the affected populations remain unrecovered.
The September 1 fires are not yet proven to have been caused by the known recall defects.
pr_vs_reality.verdict: Act on a model match immediately, but do not exaggerate the still-unproven cause of the newest incidents.
